title: A Ghost for the Protocol
premise: Hazel Pemberton, a whistle-blower living under four names, has built a career handling leaks too dangerous for anyone to claim. When a burner phone that shouldn't exist rings with the voice of her dead mentor, Elias Voss, she is drawn into his final operation: a ledger implicating the Meridian Group, the very corporation she once exposed and fled. The voice is real — Elias faked his death to become Meridian's inside ghost, and now he needs Hazel to carry the ledger out before his handlers find him. Betrayed by the one ally she trusted with her fourth name, Hazel must choose between trading the ledger — the secret worth killing for — for a seat on the dawn extraction flight, or burning it to free Elias. She trades a forged copy, keeps the truth, and walks away with Elias presumed dead again while the found family of fixers she assembled becomes the only home she'll ever claim.
about_author: Beatrix Lockridge spent a decade as an investigative producer before trading newsrooms for fiction, drawing on a lifetime of watching sources vanish into new names. She writes from a coastal town she declines to name, where she keeps her own burner phone charged.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Hazel Pemberton, working under her fourth identity as a records clerk in Rotterdam, takes an anonymous case routing documents no client will admit to owning. Her careful routines are established — cash, dead drops, no attachments. When a burner phone arrives in her dead drop, unrequested and untraceable, her paranoia spikes. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the loneliness of a life built on erasure.

chapters.title: A Voice from the Cold
chapters.summary: The phone rings: Elias Voss, her mentor who died eighteen months ago in a car fire. His voice is unmistakable, and he knows things only Elias knew. He tells her he's alive inside Meridian Group as their internal auditor-ghost, and he's assembled a ledger proving they laundered the very scandal Hazel blew the whistle on. POV: Hazel, with a flashback to Elias's 'death.' Emotional beat: grief cracking open into hope, and suspicion of both.

chapters.title: Dead Drop Protocol
chapters.summary: Elias lays out the extraction plan: a charter flight leaving a Baltic airfield at dawn in nine days, seats for two, contingent on the ledger arriving intact. Hazel tests him with questions only the real Elias could answer — and one false answer he gives, which terrifies her more than any lie. She contacts her old network: Ines the forger, Tomas the pilot, and Devi the analyst. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: cautious reassembly of a found family scattered by fear.

chapters.title: What Devi Found
chapters.summary: Devi cross-references the ledger fragments Elias transmitted and confirms the Meridian paper trail is genuine — but discovers a second file embedded within it, encrypted, addressed to Hazel by name. Meanwhile, Meridian's security chief, Ansel Roark, surfaces in Rotterdam asking quiet questions about a clerk named Hazel Pemberton. POV: alternating Hazel and Roark. Emotional beat: the hunted feeling returning; safety was always rented, never owned.

chapters.title: Ines's Hands
chapters.summary: Ines begins forging duplicate ledgers — one true, one poisoned — so Hazel can trade a copy without surrendering the original. Through the work, Ines forces Hazel to admit why she lives under four names: not just fear, but shame at what exposing Meridian cost her sister. POV: Ines, an outsider's view of Hazel. Emotional beat: intimacy forged through craft; found family as chosen accountability.

chapters.title: Roark's Offer
chapters.summary: Roark finds Hazel — not to arrest her, but to hire her back. Meridian suspects a ghost in their books and will pay handsomely for the traitor's identity; he shows her surveillance photos of Elias alive. The temptation is power offered as safety. Hazel stalls, learning Roark already knows about the dawn flight. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: corruption's seduction — power promising to end fear at the price of becoming its instrument.

chapters.title: The Encrypted File
chapters.summary: Devi cracks the embedded file: it contains evidence that Elias's death was staged with Meridian's blessing — he traded his old life for access, sacrificing the colleagues who trusted him, including a source who died in custody. Elias confesses over the phone. Hazel must decide whether the man asking for rescue is her mentor or Meridian's best product. POV: Devi, then Hazel. Emotional beat: betrayal inside inheritance — she inherited his war along with his sins.

chapters.title: Nine Hours to Dawn
chapters.summary: Roark's team raids Ines's studio; Ines burns the forgeries and escapes wounded, buying Hazel hours. Tomas moves the flight up. Elias reveals the final twist: the ledger's real value is a live account Meridian can't close without confessing — whoever holds it holds them. Roark offers Hazel everything for it. POV: rapid alternation across the network. Emotional beat: rising dread; every ally paying a price for choosing her.

chapters.title: The Trade at the Airfield
chapters.summary: At the fog-bound airfield, Hazel meets Elias face to face for the first time in two years. Roark's team closes in. Hazel executes the trade: she hands Roark the poisoned ledger, which will unravel Meridian's own cover-up when authenticated, and offers Elias the seat — but he gives it to her, staying behind to feed Roark the trail. The plane lifts at first light. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice, forgiveness, and refusing to let power buy her.

chapters.title: Dawn, Under a Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the poisoned ledger detonates publicly; Meridian's executives fall, Roark vanishes, and Elias resurfaces only as a voice on a new burner phone, alive and finally honest. Hazel buries the fourth name and chooses a fifth — but this time she shares it with Ines, Devi, and Tomas, signing their collective work with one name. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: resolution — inheritance reclaimed as legacy, power refused, family chosen.
